content:
Over the past year, we have been eagerly awaiting the next-generation iPad mini update, and good news appears to be on the horizon. Aaron Perris revealed last week that the new device will feature an A20 Pro chip and narrower display bezels, and we also know it will adopt an OLED display with a waterproof design.

While these upgrades are already quite appealing, my biggest expectation for the next iPad mini actually concerns the software side.

After watching the iPhone Duo, I have truly gained a new appreciation for Apple's multitasking capabilities. The multitasking experience on iPad has always felt quite chaotic to me, but the iPhone Duo's performance appears elegant and fluid.

On such a small screen, traditional window operations have never really suited the iPad mini. Users probably do not want to stack too many windows on it. So I hope Apple can borrow a practical feature from the iPhone Duo: split view combined with picture-in-picture.

What I mean is, this experience is truly first-class. Currently on the iPad mini, when used in portrait mode, the picture-in-picture window cannot occupy the full width of the screen; even if it could, it either obscures part of the app content, or you have to manually adjust its size through the window controls.

Bringing split video and app screens to the iPad mini's display seems like a given to me—especially considering the iPhone Duo and iPad mini have similar screen aspect ratios. At least for me personally, if this feature existed, I would use my iPad mini in portrait mode far more often.
